easy.def: How fast you move.
examples: We walked at a fast pace.
The pace is slow.
Keep the same pace.

more.def: The speed at which you walk, run or do something.
examples: We walked at a quick pace to catch the bus.
The runner kept a steady pace.
The teacher slowed the pace of the lesson.

easy.def: To walk back and forth.
examples: He paces the floor.
She paced when she was nervous.
The lion paced in its cage.

more.def: To walk back and forth in a small space, often because you are nervous.
examples: He paced the floor while waiting for the phone call.
The tiger paced back and forth in its pen.
She paced the hall before her speech.

easy.def: To put things in a bag or box.
examples: Pack your bag.
We packed for the trip.
He packs his lunch.

more.def: To put things into a bag, box or suitcase to carry them.
examples: I packed my swimsuit and towel in a bag.
Dad packs our lunches every morning.
We packed the car for the trip.

easy.def: A group of wolves or dogs.
examples: A pack of wolves howled.
The pack ran through the snow.
A pack of dogs barked.

more.def: A group of animals, such as wolves or dogs, that live or hunt together.
examples: A pack of wolves traveled across the snowy plain.
The pack of dogs ran along the beach.
Each pack of wolves has a leader.

easy.def: A small box or bag of things.
examples: I bought a pack of gum.
She opened a pack of cards.
We need a pack of pencils.

more.def: A small package that holds several of the same thing.
examples: She bought a pack of pencils for school.
A pack of cards has fifty-two cards.
Mom opened a new pack of napkins.

easy.def: A box or bag with things wrapped up inside.
examples: The mailman brought a package.
I opened the package.
The package is for you.

more.def: Something that is wrapped or put in a box so that it can be carried or mailed.
examples: A package arrived from my aunt on my birthday.
She tied string around the package before mailing it.
The package of crackers is on the shelf.

easy.def: A small package or envelope.
examples: I opened a packet of gum.
The packet is small.
She gave me a packet.

more.def: A small package or envelope that holds something.
examples: I opened a packet of seeds.
A packet of sugar sat next to the cup.
She handed out a packet of papers to each student.

easy.def: A serious promise between two or more people or groups.
examples: We made a pact.
The pact was a secret.
The friends made a pact to help each other.

more.def: A formal agreement between people or groups to do something together.
examples: The two friends made a pact to stay in touch.
The countries signed a pact to share their water.
We made a pact that we would always tell each other the truth.

easy.def: A soft cushion or a block of paper.
examples: I wear knee pads.
I wrote on a pad of paper.
The cat sat on a pad.

more.def: A soft piece of material for protection, or sheets of paper stuck together at one edge.
examples: The skater wore pads on her knees.
I wrote my name on a pad of paper.
The cat has soft pads on its paws.

easy.def: A short pole with a flat end for a boat.
examples: I hold the paddle.
The paddle is wood.
We lost a paddle.

more.def: A short pole with a flat end that is used to move a small boat through water.
examples: I dipped the paddle into the water.
The canoe has two paddles.
She lost her paddle in the river.

easy.def: To push a small boat along with a short pole.
examples: We paddle the canoe.
He paddled across the lake.
They paddled down the stream.

more.def: To move a canoe or kayak through water by pushing on a pole with a flat end.
examples: We paddled the canoe across the lake.
They paddled slowly down the stream.
I paddled to the shore.

easy.def: One side of a sheet in a book.
examples: Turn the page.
I read one page.
My book has a hundred pages.

more.def: One side of a sheet of paper in a book, magazine or newspaper.
examples: Turn to page twelve in your book.
The story ends on the last page.
Each page of the magazine has bright pictures.

easy.def: One screen on a website.
examples: The page has a picture.
Click to open the page.
This page tells about frogs.

more.def: A single screen of information on a website.
examples: The school's web page lists the lunch menu.
This page has facts about frogs and toads.
The page loaded slowly on the old computer.

easy.def: A show with costumes.
examples: The school pageant was fun.
We were in a pageant.
The holiday pageant is on Friday.

more.def: A show with costumes, music and acting, often about history or a holiday.
examples: The school held a holiday pageant.
She wore a costume in the town pageant.
The pageant told the story of the town.

easy.def: A small device that beeps to tell you to call someone.
examples: The nurse's pager beeped.
He has a pager on his belt.
A pager buzzed in the room.

more.def: A small device that people carry, which beeps or buzzes to tell them to call someone or come to a place.
examples: The doctor's pager beeped, so she hurried back to the hospital.
In the 1990s, many workers carried a pager on their belts.
The restaurant gave us a pager that buzzed when our table was ready.

easy.def: A hurting feeling.
examples: I feel pain in my knee.
The shot caused a little pain.
He cried out in pain.

more.def: A feeling of hurt in the body.
examples: I felt a sharp pain in my foot.
The medicine took away the pain.
She had a pain in her tooth.

easy.def: Hurting.
examples: My sore toe is painful.
The shot was painful.
It is painful to walk.

more.def: Causing pain or hurting a lot.
examples: The splinter in my finger was painful.
Walking on the hot sand was painful.
A sunburn can be painful.

easy.def: Colored liquid you put on things.
examples: The paint is wet.
I need red paint.
We used paint on the wall.

more.def: A colored liquid used to cover a surface or make pictures.
examples: Dad put a coat of blue paint on the fence.
The paint on the art table was still wet.
She mixed yellow and blue paint to make green.

easy.def: To cover something with color.
examples: I paint a picture.
We painted the fence.
She paints flowers.

more.def: To cover a surface with colored liquid, or to make a picture with it.
examples: The class painted a mural on the wall.
He painted the barn red.
She likes to paint the sea.

easy.def: A person who paints pictures.
examples: The painter has a brush.
A painter painted the sea.
She is a painter.

more.def: A person who paints pictures as art.
examples: The painter used bright colors.
A famous painter made this picture.
The painter set up her easel by the sea.

easy.def: A person who paints walls.
examples: The painter painted the room.
A painter came to the house.
The painter used a roller.

more.def: A person whose job is to paint walls and buildings.
examples: The painter painted the kitchen yellow.
A house painter climbed the ladder.
The painters covered the floor with sheets.

easy.def: A picture made with paint.
examples: The painting is pretty.
She made a painting.
A painting hangs on the wall.

more.def: A picture made with paint, such as one on a canvas or wall.
examples: A painting of a barn hung on the wall.
The museum has an old painting of a ship.
She finished her painting of the sunset.

easy.def: Two things that go together.
examples: I have a pair of shoes.
A pair of socks.
We are a pair.

more.def: Two things of the same kind that are used together.
examples: She bought a new pair of shoes.
A pair of scissors lay on the table.
The two friends walked as a pair.

easy.def: Clothes you wear to bed.
examples: I wear pajamas to bed.
My pajamas have stars.
She put on her pajamas.

more.def: Loose pants and a top that you wear to sleep in.
examples: I put on my pajamas and brushed my teeth.
My pajamas have little stars.
He wore his pajamas to breakfast.

easy.def: A friend.
examples: He is my pal.
My pal and I play ball.
She is a good pal.

more.def: A close and friendly companion.
examples: My pal and I walk to school together.
He is a loyal pal who always helps.
She wrote to her pen pal.

easy.def: A big home of a king or queen.
examples: The queen lives in a palace.
The palace is huge.
We visited a palace.

more.def: A very large and grand home of a king, queen or other ruler.
examples: The king lived in a golden palace.
We toured the palace and saw the royal rooms.
The palace had hundreds of rooms and a huge garden.

easy.def: Light in color.
examples: Her face was pale.
The pale blue sky.
I like pale yellow.

more.def: Light in color, or not bright.
examples: She looked pale after being sick.
The walls were painted a pale blue.
A pale moon rose over the lake.

easy.def: The inside part of your hand.
examples: I held the coin in my palm.
My palm is sweaty.
She put a seed in her palm.

more.def: The flat inside part of your hand, between your wrist and fingers.
examples: He held the coin in the palm of his hand.
A tiny frog sat in her palm.
I clapped my palms together.

easy.def: A tall tree with big leaves at the top.
examples: A palm grows on the beach.
The palm tree is tall.
Coconuts grow on a palm.

more.def: A tall tree that grows in warm places and has a bunch of large leaves at the top.
examples: Palm trees waved in the breeze at the beach.
A palm tree gave shade to the whole picnic.
We sat in the shade of a palm.

easy.def: A flat dish for cooking.
examples: Mom cooked eggs in a pan.
The pan is hot.
I washed the pan.

more.def: A flat, wide container with a handle that is used for cooking.
examples: Mom cooked pancakes in a pan.
The pan was too hot to touch.
He washed the frying pan.

easy.def: A flat, round cake that you cook in a pan.
examples: I eat pancakes.
The pancake is round.
Dad flipped a pancake.

more.def: A thin, flat cake made of batter and cooked in a pan, often eaten at breakfast.
examples: We had pancakes and syrup for breakfast.
Dad flipped the pancake in the air.
She stacked three pancakes on her plate.

easy.def: A flat piece that is part of a wall, door or machine.
examples: The door has a panel.
The panel is glass.
A panel opened.

more.def: A flat, square piece that forms part of a wall, door or control board.
examples: The door has a glass panel.
Dad opened the panel on the wall.
The control panel had many buttons.

easy.def: A group of people who talk or judge.
examples: The panel chose the winner.
A panel of judges sat at the table.
The panel talked about the books.

more.def: A small group of people chosen to talk about something or make a decision.
examples: A panel of judges chose the winner.
The panel talked about the importance of reading.
The students sat on a panel to answer questions.

easy.def: Sudden, wild fear.

Panic spread.

more.def: A sudden feeling of fear that makes you act without thinking.
examples: Panic spread through the crowd when the lights went out.
She felt panic when she lost her mom in the store.

easy.def: To be so afraid you cannot think.
examples: Do not panic.
The crowd panicked.
She panicked.

more.def: To feel sudden fear and not think clearly.
examples: Stay calm and do not panic.
The crowd panicked when the alarm rang.
He panicked when he could not find his keys.

easy.def: To breathe fast with your mouth open.

The puppy panted.

more.def: To breathe quickly and loudly, especially after running or in heat.
examples: The dog panted in the heat.
I panted after the race.

easy.def: A big black cat that lives in forests.

A black panther is in the story.
The panther climbed a tree.

more.def: A large, wild cat with a black coat, or a leopard or cougar.
examples: The black panther crept through the forest.
A panther can climb trees and swim in rivers.

easy.def: Clothes that cover both legs.
examples: I wear pants to school.
My pants are blue.
Put on your pants.

more.def: A piece of clothing that covers the body from the waist to the ankles, with a separate part for each leg.
examples: He wore warm pants in the snow.
My pants have deep pockets.
She rolled up her pants to wade in the creek.

easy.def: A name for a father.

more.def: A word that some children use for their father.

easy.def: Thin, flat sheets for writing and drawing.

She folded a sheet of paper into a bird.
Put the used paper in the recycling bin.

easy.def: A newspaper.
examples: Dad reads the paper.
The paper came this morning.

more.def: A set of printed pages of news that comes out each day or week.

easy.def: Forms and papers that must be filled in.

more.def: Written forms and records that have to be filled in or kept.
examples: Dad has a lot of paperwork to do.
The nurse filled in the paperwork.

easy.def: Normal or average.

more.def: The usual or average level, or the number of hits a golfer should need for a hole.
examples: Her work is above par this term.
He feels a little below par today.

easy.def: A big cloth that opens up so you float down slowly.

more.def: A large piece of light cloth that opens up in the air so a person or object can float slowly down.

more.def: To drop or float down from the sky using a large cloth that opens above you.
examples: The skydivers parachuted onto the wide green field.
Food was parachuted to the people after the flood.

easy.def: A line of people, bands or floats that moves along a street.

The parade has a band.

more.def: A show in which bands, floats and people move along a street for people to watch.
examples: We watched the parade on the Fourth of July.
The band marched in the parade.

easy.def: A perfect place.

The beach was paradise.
A garden paradise.

more.def: A place that is as beautiful and perfect as you could wish.
examples: The island felt like a paradise.
The beach was a paradise for the kids.

easy.def: A group of sentences about one idea.

Read the first paragraph.
Each paragraph starts on a new line.

more.def: A part of a piece of writing made up of several sentences about one idea, which usually starts on a new line.

easy.def: A mother or father.

more.def: A mother or father, or someone who takes care of a child as they would.

easy.def: Taking care of a child as a mom or dad.

easy.def: A place outside with grass and trees to play.

more.def: A public place with grass, trees and often playgrounds, where people go to play and relax.

easy.def: To take part.

easy.def: Having a very strong feeling for something.

more.def: Farther than, or on the other side of something.
examples: Go past the bakery and turn left.
The bus drove past our house without stopping.
She ran past the finish line.

easy.def: Noodles, like spaghetti.
examples: I love pasta.
We ate pasta for dinner.
The pasta is in the pot.

more.def: A food made from flour and water that is cooked in boiling water, such as spaghetti or macaroni.
examples: We had pasta with tomato sauce for dinner.
Dad boiled the pasta until it was soft.
Spaghetti, penne and macaroni are all kinds of pasta.

easy.def: A person who leads a church.
examples: The pastor gave a talk.
Our pastor is kind.
The pastor greeted us.

more.def: A leader of a church, who takes care of the people who worship there.
examples: The pastor welcomed everyone to the church.
Our pastor gave a short talk about being kind to others.
The pastor helped organize the church food drive.

easy.def: A field where cows or sheep eat grass.
examples: The cows are in the pasture.
Sheep ate in the pasture.
The pasture is green.

more.def: A field of grass where farm animals such as cows, horses and sheep are kept to eat.
examples: The cows wandered across the pasture, munching the grass as they went.
The farmer moved the sheep to a new pasture by the river.
Horses galloped through the pasture in the morning mist.

easy.def: A piece put over a hole to fix it.
examples: Mom put a patch on my jeans.
The patch is blue.
A patch covers the hole.

more.def: A small piece of material used to cover a hole or a worn place.
examples: Grandma sewed a patch on the knee of my jeans.
A rubber patch fixed the hole in the tire.
The old quilt was made from many colorful patches.

easy.def: A small area that is different from the rest.
examples: A patch of grass was brown.
There is a patch of ice.
A patch of flowers grew by the fence.

more.def: A small area that is different from what is around it.
examples: A patch of ice made the road slippery.
We picked pumpkins from the pumpkin patch.
A patch of blue sky showed between the clouds.

easy.def: Cloth made by sewing many small pieces together.
examples: The quilt is patchwork.
Grandma made a patchwork.
I like patchwork.

more.def: Cloth made by sewing together many small pieces of different cloth.
examples: Grandma made a patchwork quilt from old shirts.
The patchwork pillow had squares of every color.
From the airplane, the fields looked like a green and gold patchwork.

easy.def: A narrow way to walk along.
examples: We walked on a path in the woods.
The path leads to the lake.
A path of stones led to the door.

more.def: A narrow track for people or animals to walk along.
examples: The hikers followed a muddy path up the hill.
Deer made a path through the tall grass.
A garden path winds between the flower beds.

easy.def: So weak or sad that it makes you feel sorry.
examples: The kitten was wet and pathetic.
A pathetic little cry came from the box.
The old toy looked pathetic.

more.def: Sad and weak in a way that makes people feel sorry.
examples: The soaked puppy looked pathetic in the rain.
The fire gave only a pathetic little flame.
He made a pathetic try to lift the heavy box.

easy.def: Being able to wait without getting upset.
examples: She has a lot of patience.
Learning takes patience.
I lost my patience.

more.def: The ability to stay calm while waiting or when something is hard.
examples: Teaching a puppy to sit takes patience.
She waited with patience for her turn.
Fishing takes a lot of patience.

easy.def: Able to wait without getting upset.
examples: Be patient. It will be your turn soon.
The patient dog waited for its food.
Be patient while the cake bakes.

more.def: Able to stay calm while waiting or when something is hard.
examples: The patient teacher explained the problem again until everyone understood.
You must be patient when you are fishing.
She is patient with her little brother when he learns new games.

easy.def: Calmly, while waiting.
examples: The dog waited patiently.
She patiently stood in line.
He patiently explained.

more.def: In a calm way that does not get upset by waiting or problems.
examples: The dog waited patiently by the door.
She stood patiently in line.
He patiently explained the rules again.

easy.def: A flat, hard area outside a house, for sitting.
examples: We ate lunch on the patio.
The patio is outside.
They put chairs on the patio.

more.def: A flat, paved area beside a house, used for sitting, eating or relaxing outdoors.
examples: We ate dinner outside on the patio on warm summer evenings.
Dad swept the leaves off the patio.
Pots of flowers lined the edge of the patio.

easy.def: A person who loves and supports their country.
examples: A patriot loves the flag.
He is a patriot.
The patriot sang the anthem.

more.def: A person who loves their country and wants to help it.
examples: A patriot cares about the good of the whole country.
In the history book, we read about patriots who helped found the nation.
The patriot stood proudly while the band played the anthem.

easy.def: To walk or drive around to keep a place safe.
examples: The guard patrols the building.
The officer patrols the street.
The ranger patrols the park.

more.def: To go around an area to watch it and keep it safe.
examples: The ranger patrols the park every morning.
Guards patrolled the museum at night.
The police patrol our neighborhood.

easy.def: A group that goes around to keep a place safe.
examples: A patrol came by.
The patrol checked the park.
The sea patrol saved the boat.

more.def: A person or group sent around an area to watch over it.
examples: The park patrol checked the trail.
A police patrol drove down the street.
The ship sent out a patrol.

easy.def: Shapes, colors, or things that repeat again and again.
examples: My shirt has a pattern of red and blue dots.
The rug has a pattern of stars.
Clap the pattern with me.

more.def: A design or set of things that repeats in a regular way.
examples: Can you find the pattern in these numbers: 2, 4, 6, 8?
The tiles made a pattern of blue and white squares.
Scientists look for patterns in the weather.

easy.def: To stop for a short time.
examples: Pause the video.
She paused at the door.
The band paused.

more.def: To stop for a short time before going on.
examples: Pause the video while I get a snack.
She paused at the door and listened.
The speaker paused to take a sip of water.

easy.def: A short stop.
examples: There was a pause.
The pause was long.
He took a pause.

more.def: A short break in speaking or doing something.
examples: There was a long pause after her question.
The pause gave us time to think.
The band took a short pause between songs.

easy.def: An animal's foot.
examples: The dog has a muddy paw.
The cat's paw is soft.
The bear's paw is big.

more.def: The foot of an animal such as a cat, dog or bear, with claws or pads.
examples: The dog left muddy paw prints on the floor.
The cat licked its paw.
The bear's huge paw swiped at the log.

easy.def: The smallest chess piece.
examples: I moved a pawn.
The pawn is in front.
A pawn moves forward.

more.def: The smallest and most common piece in the game of chess.
examples: I moved a pawn forward.
The pawn can capture a piece on a slant.
He lost a pawn in the game.

easy.def: To give money for something.
examples: I pay for the toy.
Dad paid the bill.
She pays with coins.

more.def: To give money in return for something you buy or for work that was done.
examples: We paid for our tickets at the door.
The bakery pays its workers every Friday.
I used my savings to pay for the new bike.

easy.def: Something done to get even with someone.
examples: He wanted payback.
It was payback for the prank.
She took her payback.

more.def: Something done to someone because they did something to you.
examples: The prank was payback for the one he played last week.
It is better to forgive than to seek payback.
In the story, the clever fox got payback on the crow.

easy.def: Money for work.
examples: Dad got a paycheck.
The paycheck comes on Friday.
She cashed her paycheck.

more.def: A check or payment that a worker gets for their work.
examples: Dad got his paycheck on Friday.
She put her paycheck in the bank.
The paycheck was bigger this month.

easy.def: Money you give for something.
examples: Make a payment.
The payment was due.
He made a payment on the car.

more.def: An amount of money that you give to pay for something.
examples: Dad made a payment on the car.
We got the bill and sent a payment.
The shop takes cash as payment.

easy.def: A good result from hard work.
examples: The payoff was a big prize.
Hard work has a big payoff.
The payoff was worth it.

more.def: A reward or good result that you get from your effort or from taking a chance.
examples: After weeks of practice, the payoff was winning the school spelling bee.
Planting seeds takes patience, but the payoff is fresh tomatoes in the summer.
The long hike had a great payoff: a view of the whole valley.
